news.headline: Kindergarteners Find a Super-Rare Spider
news.body: During an outdoor learning day at their school in Michigan, a class of kindergarteners lifted a rock and found a big, dark brown spider. Their teachers didn't know what it was, so they asked an expert at Michigan State University. He said it was a folding-door spider, one of the hardest spiders in the state to find! These spiders live in tunnels underground and build a little door out of silk and dirt that blends right in. Before this, only three had been spotted in Michigan on a popular nature app.

news.headline: NASA's Flying Robot Practices Its First Flight
news.body: NASA is building a car-sized flying robot called Dragonfly that will explore Titan, Saturn's biggest moon. This week, engineers tested its very first flight, but on computers here on Earth! In the practice run, Dragonfly zoomed over sand dunes, scanned the ground for a safe spot, circled back, and landed all by itself. Dragonfly is planned to launch no earlier than 2028 and reach Titan in 2034. Then it will spend three years hopping from place to place to learn about this strange moon.

news.headline: Students Plant a Tiny Forest at School
news.body: Fourth graders at a school in Australia spent a whole week planting about 1,000 native plants in a bare patch of their playground. They are making a microforest, a thick little forest about the size of a tennis court. The plants are packed close together, which helps them grow up to 10 times faster than normal. In just two or three years, the forest could be about 23 feet tall! It will give the kids shade and make a home for birds, bugs, and other wildlife.

fun_fact: Titan, Saturn's biggest moon, is larger than the planet Mercury. It's also the only moon in our solar system with a thick blanket of air! 🪐

this_day_in_history: On October 25, 1881, the famous artist Pablo Picasso was born in Spain. He made more than 20,000 paintings, drawings, and sculptures in his life! 🎨
did_you_know: Trees can talk to each other, sort of! Their roots connect underground through tiny threads of fungus that pass along water and food. 🍄
